page: Amazon Web Services c5a.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring AMD EPYC 7R32 processors. The instance provides 48 vCPUs mapped across 24 dedicated physical cores with multithreading, running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 96 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard compute-optimized memory-to-core ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA, although it lacks AVX-512 extensions. No dedicated GPUs or local NVMe storage are bundled with this instance type, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c5a.12xlarge solidly within average performance ranges across most standard server evaluations. Single-core throughput exhibits lower relative efficiency, as seen in stress-ng single-core tests (762.49, bottom 10%), but the aggregate thread capacity delivers balanced scaling in multi-core metrics, scoring 18392.86 on stress-ng multi-core and 12873.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Cryptographic throughput is an operational highlight due to integrated hardware primitives, achieving a strong PassMark CPU encryption score of 51158.65 (top 25%). Memory operations are similarly performant, registering a PassMark memory score of 2874.09 (top 25%) and uncached read bandwidth of 96.05 GB/s on 256 MB blocks.

The compute profile favors distributed, multi-threaded workloads that execute parallel instructions efficiently without requiring massive individual thread frequencies or localized high-speed NVMe scratch volumes. The combination of 48 dedicated threads, stable 12 Gbps networking, and balanced 96 GB memory pool makes this instance suitable for batch processing pipelines, CI/CD compilation farms, static web clusters, distributed data transformation (ETL), and scale-out application tiers.
